title: CEOs and execs can't agree on what AI means for Gen Z workers
excerpt: For young Gen Zers entering the workforce, the rise of generative artificial intelligence has brought no shortage of uncertainty.
content_html:
For young Gen Zers entering the workforce, the rise of generative artificial intelligence has brought no shortage of uncertainty.

Anthropic's CEO has warned that the tech could wipe out many entry-level roles, while other executives have argued that younger employees may be better positioned than anyone to thrive in an AI-powered workplace.

The debate underscores one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding AI: Will it eliminate the first rung of the career ladder, or help young job hunters climb it faster?

"I think a lot of the disagreement is centered around the speed that the AI transition will take place," Felix Aidala, an economist at the Indeed Hiring Lab, the job platform's economic research arm, told Business Insider.

Entry-level job postings on Indeed have fallen about 6% over the past year, though Aidala said it's difficult to attribute the decline to any single factor. AI, remote work, and broader macroeconomic conditions have likely all played a role, he said.

Aidala added that the job market for entry-level workers is already seeing some "AI-driven shifts," with AI implementation roles growing "significantly" on Indeed's site in recent months.

"Historically, technological advancements have almost always led to job growth for the economy as a whole. But those transformations take time as new roles and industries are developed," Aidala said.

Here's what some CEOs and executives in tech and business have said about what AI means for the next generation of workers.

Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has become one of the leading voices warning that AI could upend the traditional career ladder for young professionals.

Amodei has repeatedly said that AI may eliminate up to half of entry-level white-collar jobs over the next several years.

"We, as the producers of this technology, have a duty and an obligation to be honest about what is coming," Amodei said in an interview last year.

Matt Garman, CEO of Amazon Web Services

Amazon cloud chief Matt Garman has taken almost the opposite view, saying that doomsday predictions about AI and jobs are way overblown.

Garman has said that he believes half of white-collar jobs "may change" because of AI, but that doesn't mean they'll disappear. He has also called the idea of replacing entry-level staff with AI tools "one of the dumbest things" he's ever heard.

Speaking on a recent episode of the Platformer podcast, Garman stressed the value of entry-level employees, saying they're inexpensive to hire, can be taught a company's culture, and are often eager to learn new tools.

"They're some of the very best employees you can possibly have," he said.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

Sam Altman, the CEO of ChatGPT creator OpenAI, recently said AI has not yet displaced entry-level white-collar workers as quickly as he expected.

"I'm delighted to be wrong about this," he said at an event hosted by the Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "I thought that there would have been more impact on entry-level white-collar work jobs being eliminated by now than it's actually happened."

Elizabeth Stone, Netflix's chief product and technology officer

Even as AI transforms how work gets done, Netflix's chief product and technology officer, Elizabeth Stone, said junior employees remain essential to the streaming giant's future.

"We are still hiring junior people, and they're really important to our talent strategy," Stone recently said on an episode of "Lenny's Podcast."

Younger employees, she said, can be more open-minded, more comfortable with emerging AI technologies, and more attuned to how entertainment is changing.

"I can guarantee you that earlier career talent is going to be teaching older folks like me many new things, too," Stone said.

Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis' advice for young people preparing to enter the workforce is: become an AI "ninja."

Hassabis has urged teenagers and students to immerse themselves in AI tools, arguing that those who master the technology early will have a leg up as AI disrupts the job market.

"Whatever happens with these AI tools, you'll be better off understanding how they work, and how they function, and what you can do with them," Hassabis said last year on an episode of "Hard Fork."

Garrett Lord, CEO of Handshake

Garrett Lord, the CEO of job search and AI training platform Handshake, said on an episode of "Lenny's Podcast" last year that new graduates are well equipped to succeed because they're "AI native."

Knowing how to use AI is like "having your Iron Man suit on," Lord said.

"A lot of people are kind of hyperbolic at saying that all young people won't have jobs," Lord said, adding, "That's not what we're hearing from our employers."

Sierra cofounder Clay Bavor

Clay Bavor, the cofounder of Sierra, an AI startup that builds customer service agents, has made a similar case, arguing that AI-native graduates are entering the workforce with a built-in advantage.

Speaking on a recent episode of the "20VC" podcast, Bavor said some of the company's strongest employees are in their early 20s because they're more adept at using AI than many veteran workers.

"I can't remember a time when a young person with no work experience, but with the right mindset and experience using some of these tools, has ever been so valued," Bavor said.

content_html_zh:
对于进入职场的年轻 Z 世代来说，生成型人工智能的兴起带来了不乏不确定性。

Anthropic 的首席执行官警告称，这项技术可能会消除许多初级职位，而其他高管则认为，年轻员工可能比任何人都更有能力在人工智能驱动的工作场所中蓬勃发展。

这场辩论凸显了围绕人工智能的一个尚未解答的最大问题：它会消除职业阶梯的第一级，还是帮助年轻的求职者更快地攀登？

“我认为，很多分歧都集中在人工智能转型的速度上，”该就业平台的经济研究机构 Indeed 招聘实验室的经济学家菲利克斯·艾达拉 (Felix Aidala) 告诉《商业内幕》。

过去一年中，Indeed 上的入门级职位发布量下降了约 6%，不过艾达拉表示很难将这一下降归因于任何单一因素。 他说，人工智能、远程工作和更广泛的宏观经济条件可能都发挥了作用。

Aidala 补充说，入门级员工的就业市场已经出现了一些“人工智能驱动的转变”，近几个月来 Indeed 网站上的人工智能实施角色“显着”增长。

“从历史上看，技术进步几乎总是会带来整个经济的就业增长。 但随着新角色和行业的发展，这些转变需要时间，”艾达拉说。

以下是一些科技和商业领域的首席执行官和高管对于人工智能对下一代工人意味着什么的看法。

达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei)，Anthropic 首席执行官

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 已成为警告人工智能可能颠覆年轻专业人士传统职业阶梯的主要声音之一。

阿莫代一再表示，人工智能可能会在未来几年内消除多达一半的入门级白领工作。

阿莫迪在去年的一次采访中表示：“作为这项技术的生产者，我们有责任和义务诚实地面对即将发生的事情。”

马特·加曼 (Matt Garman)，亚马逊网络服务首席执行官

亚马逊云业务负责人马特·加曼(Matt Garman)持几乎相反的观点，他表示有关人工智能和就业的世界末日预测过于夸大了。

加曼表示，他相信一半的白领工作“可能会因为人工智能而改变”，但这并不意味着它们会消失。 他还称用人工智能工具取代初级员工的想法是他听过的“最愚蠢的事情之一”。

加曼在平台游戏播客最近一集的讲话中强调了初级员工的价值，称他们的雇佣成本低廉，可以学习公司文化，并且往往渴望学习新工具。

“他们是你能拥有的最优秀的员工之一，”他说。

OpenAI 首席执行官山姆·奥尔特曼

ChatGPT 创建者 OpenAI 的首席执行官 Sam Altman 最近表示，人工智能尚未像他预期的那样快速取代入门级白领工人。

他在澳大利亚联邦银行主办的一次活动上表示：“我很高兴在这一点上犯了错误。” “我认为现在被淘汰的入门级白领工作岗位所产生的影响会比实际发生的影响更大。”

伊丽莎白·斯通 (Elizabeth Stone)，Netflix 首席产品和技术官

尽管人工智能改变了工作方式，Netflix 首席产品和技术官伊丽莎白·斯通 (Elizabeth Stone) 表示，初级员工对于这家流媒体巨头的未来仍然至关重要。

“我们仍在招聘初级人才，他们对我们的人才战略非常重要，”斯通最近在“莱尼播客”的一集中说道。

她说，年轻员工的思想更加开放，更能适应新兴的人工智能技术，也更能适应娱乐业的变化。

斯通说：“我可以向你保证，早期职业人才也会教给像我这样的老年人许多新东西。”

谷歌 DeepMind 首席执行官 Demis Hassabis

谷歌 DeepMind 首席执行官 Demis Hassabis 对准备进入职场的年轻人的建议是：成为一名 AI“忍者”。

哈萨比斯敦促青少年和学生沉浸在人工智能工具中，他认为，随着人工智能扰乱就业市场，那些尽早掌握该技术的人将占据优势。

哈萨比斯去年在“硬分叉”节目中表示：“无论这些人工智能工具发生什么，你都会更好地了解它们的工作原理、功能以及可以用它们做什么。”

加勒特·洛德 (Garrett Lord)，Handshake 首席执行官

求职和人工智能培训平台 Handshake 的首席执行官加勒特·洛德 (Garrett Lord) 去年在“Lenny's Podcast”的一集中表示，应届毕业生完全有能力取得成功，因为他们是“人工智能原生者”。

洛德说，了解如何使用人工智能就像“穿上钢铁侠战衣”。

洛德说：“很多人都有点夸张地说，所有年轻人都不会找到工作。”他补充道，“这并不是我们从雇主那里听到的说法。”

Sierra 联合创始人 Clay Bavor

建立客户服务代理的人工智能初创公司 Sierra 的联合创始人克莱·巴沃尔 (Clay Bavor) 也提出了类似的案例，认为人工智能本土毕业生正在以固有的优势进入劳动力市场。

Bavor 在最近一期的“20VC”播客中表示，该公司一些最优秀的员工都在 20 岁出头，因为他们比许多资深员工更擅长使用人工智能。

巴沃尔说：“我不记得任何时候，一个没有工作经验，但拥有正确心态和使用其中一些工具的经验的年轻人曾受到如此重视。”
